Oliver La Farge, Laughing Boy.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/oliver-la-farge/laughing-boy

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Oliver La Farge, the author and the writer of an introduction, died 1963 (Wikidata Q761453, P570 = 1963-08-02; Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_La_Farge).

First publication of the text used: 'Laughing Boy was published in 1929 by Oliver La Farge.' (SE colophon).

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1929 by Houghton Mifflin in the United States (Wikipedia: country United States, publisher Houghton Mifflin, publication year 1929). A work published in 1929 entered the United States public domain on 1 January 2025, and Standard Ebooks states the same in its rights statement (below).
- Country of origin: the United States, the country of first publication (see the US paragraph above). So the US rule also settles the country of origin, whatever the death year. La Farge died in 1963 (Wikidata Q761453, P570 = 1963-08-02), which would not pass a life + 70 test in the United Kingdom or Canada.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
